scenes.say: Ever wonder how Spring handles transactions behind the scenes? And what can go wrong if you’re not careful?

scenes.label: Propagation
scenes.sub: Controls if a method joins or starts a transaction
scenes.say: Propagation decides if your method joins an existing transaction or starts a brand new one.
Isolation levels control what data one transaction can see from another. Lower isolation is faster but riskier. Higher isolation is safer, but may slow things down.

scenes.question: What happens if a method calls itself?
scenes.right: Self-invocation skips the proxy, so @Transactional is ignored.
scenes.say: Here’s a classic trap: if a transactional method calls another transactional method in the same class, the annotation is ignored. That can break your transaction logic.
To avoid this, move the called method to another bean and inject it. That way, the transactional proxy does its job.
